scope: Quake III routing started each area cache from a stack array of 128 zero travel times read by the index of each link into the goal area, which can be entered by more links; the row is now as long as the most links into any area. Retail disassembly of nine engines, an offline measurement of every installed Quake III, Quake Live and Elite Force navigation file, fixtures that fail before the change, and bot map loads before and after on the stable win32-dev binaries.

change.rule: AAS_CreateReversedReachability allocates aasworld.startareatraveltimes, zeroed, as long as the most reversed links into any area (at least 1); AAS_FreeRoutingCaches frees it; AAS_UpdateAreaRoutingCache starts a goal area there for every profile but RTCW, whose branch still starts from aasworld.areatraveltimes[goal][0] and never allocates the row.
change.identicalAtOrUnder128: entries 0 to links-1 of the goal row are read, and are zero both in the old array and in the new row

retail.method: capstone disassembly of each installed executable; AAS_UpdateAreaRoutingCache found by the counter AAS_RoutingInfo prints ("%d area cache updates") and the function that increments it. Reference observation only; nothing from the binaries is reproduced.

engines.frame: sub esp,0x120; ebx, ebp, esi, edi pushed
engines.rowRead: mov cx,[ecx+ebx] at 0x0049EE7A, byte offset +2 a link at 0x0049EF32, no bound; the loop ends at the last reversed link (0x0049EF41)
engines.pastTheRow: the array ends at the return address: entries 128 and 129 are 0xF066 and 0x0049 of 0x0049F066, after the only call (0x0049F061, in AAS_GetAreaRoutingCache); 130 and 131 the cache pointer argument; then the caller's frame
engines.source: string "area %d has more than 128 reachabilities" (0x004D6BC4) pushed at 0x0049DE06 in AAS_CreateReversedReachability; numareacacheupdates (0x00C68868) incremented at 0x0049EC86

retail.inference: quake3.exe 1.32, quakelive_steam.exe, jamp.exe and jk2mp.exe route through links past the 128th with whatever their stacks hold there; stvoyHM.exe, et.exe, etded.exe, WolfSP.exe and WolfMP.exe cannot, since their goal row has an entry for each link, but they add travel times within the goal area that Quake III 1.32 made zero.

cases.name: test_a_goal_entered_by_more_than_128_links_routes_as_one_entered_by_fewer
cases.checks: for each profile routing as Quake III does (7), worlds with the goal or a portal entered by more links (fillers making 128 and 129 links, 200 and 1,000 fillers), 3 or 6 core areas, seeds 1 to 4: every named area's route to the goal and the portal, with and without an origin, under three sets of travel flags, equals the same world without fillers; each filler's one link costs the cache's start plus its own time

cases.name: test_links_past_the_128th_read_no_stack_under_a_guard

note: Retail travel times through links past the 128th are not reproduced: they came from stack words that differ by build, call and, in Quake Live, by process.
No bot was made to route to one of these areas at runtime; the loads show only that navigation, routing and the bot come up as before.

Elite Force Holomatch and Enemy Territory still start from zeros here, as Quake III 1.32 does, not from the goal area's first row as stvoyHM.exe, et.exe and etded.exe do; that difference applies to every goal and is left open. Elite Force's single-player engine has no bot library to compare.
